newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen up .20-.50 cent, feeders up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen up .20-.50 cent, feeders up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were called mostly 0.20 to 0.50 cent per lb higher at the opening supported by USDA's reporting of fewer hogs on U.S. farms than analysts expected, analysts said.
"The competition from pork this summer and fall will not be substantial," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.
Feeder cattle were called steady to 0.20 cent higher following expected higher live cattle. Some analysts said feeder cattle may trade in a narrow range until CBOT corn futures open at 0930 CDT.
The latest CME feeder index was up $0.64 to $79.08 per cwt.

Analysts said they doubt live cattle futures will receive much support from the cash cattle and beef markets. Some believe feedlot cattle will be bid steady to $1.00 per cwt lower at $62.00 to $63.00 this week. The holiday-shortened slaughter week may discourage meat packers from aggressively bidding for cattle, they said.
